subject: SIG/CAIQ evidence request — telemetry provenance, de-identification, and keystore rotation

Subject: SIG/CAIQ evidence request — telemetry retention & de-id

Hi Kimberly,

ComfortAI is working through SIG/CAIQ follow-ups as part of our procurement checklist. We need a concise evidence packet that covers the following for Redwood:

- Inventory of telemetry streams (ingestion, debug/traces, application logs, metrics) and the default retention for each stream.
- Description of pseudonymization/de-identification applied to telemetry (what fields, algorithmic approach, reversible vs irreversible).
- Keystore/secret rotation cadence and proof-of-rotation artifacts for the past 12 months.
- Proof-of-delete workflow and examples (for tenant-scoped deletions and customer-specific exceptions).
- CAIQ control mapping for data retention and disposal (controls mapping to your SOC2 scope).

Can you provide these materials as a single packet (attachments + short narrative) and indicate who will sign an attestation for proof-of-delete? We have a CA procurement deadline next Friday and would like the packet by EOD Thu, 16 Jul if possible.

I've attached our SIG spreadsheet with the specific questions we flagged (comfortai-sig-questions.xlsx). If you want to propose a short call for clarifications, we can do 7/17 morning PT.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Patel
Senior Security Program Manager, ComfortAI

Jordan — thanks for the clear ask and for the spreadsheet. We're on it. Two quick clarifying questions so we scope exactly what to include:

1) Which telemetry streams do you want in scope for the packet? Our common split is: ingestion traces (full request/response traces), application logs (structured events), debug/traces (developer session traces), and metrics (aggregated counters/gauges).

2) Do you need raw sample artifacts (we can redact) or redacted examples only? For keystore rotation and proof-of-delete we'll provide signed manifests and audit log snippets rather than full private keys.

Tentative plan: Ben will prepare the technical narrative (pseudonymization approach, retention table, keystore rotation cadence + artifacts), Marissa will prepare an attestation template and CAIQ control mapping language. We can aim to deliver a packaged ZIP by end of day 2026-07-17 if you can accept EOD Fri; we can accelerate to Thu EOD if you confirm scope today.

Also looping in Alicia Rana from your note — confirm if she needs to be on the attestation.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: SIG/CAIQ evidence request — telemetry retention & de-id

Kim / Jordan — adding the technical summary below and attaching the artifacts we will include.

Attachment stubs: telemetry-deid-and-rotation-2026-07.pdf (technical narrative), keystore-rotation-schedule.csv (rotation timestamps and key versions), pseudonymization-mapping-sample.txt (redacted mapping example).

Summary (for packet):
- Telemetry inventory and defaults:
  * Ingestion traces: default retention 7 days (raw request/response), 30 days (indexed) for live hosted tenants; option to extend to 90/365 via dedicated plan.
  * Application logs (structured events): default 30 days; can be scoped per-tenant for longer retention under customer request and contract.
  * Debug/traces (developer session traces): ephemeral by default — 72 hours; retained longer only if customer authorizes or under forensic/legal hold.
  * Metrics: aggregated, retained 13 months for analytics (roll-ups).

- De-identification/pseudonymization approach:
  * We apply tokenization/pseudonymization at ingestion for known PII fields (email, phone, user_id) using per-tenant salt + HMAC-SHA256 for irreversible tokens by default.
  * For customers that need reversible linkage for debugging, we support a customer-specific reversible wrapping key stored in a separate keystore with strict ACLs; enabling reversible mapping is an opt-in and tracked.
  * No plaintext secrets or raw keys are stored in telemetry. Debug traces that contain sensitive BLOBs are automatically redacted at ingestion by pattern matching and content scanning.

- Keystore / rotation cadence and artifacts:
  * Master keystore rotates keys on a 90-day cadence for platform keys; tenant wrapping keys can be configured by the customer and are rotated per customer policy.
  * Attached rotation csv shows key version ids, rotation timestamps, and signatures from our KMS (redacted key ids).
  * Proof-of-rotation artifacts: rotation manifest entries and signatures (we will provide signed manifests and KMS audit log excerpts; private key material never attached).

- Proof-of-delete workflow:
  * Customer deletion request pipeline: intake -> verification -> scoped purge job -> audit log entry -> attestation generation.
  * For tenant-scoped deletions we run a three-stage purge (index tombstone, blob purge, verification sampling) and produce a signed manifest of deleted object ids and audit log entries.
  * For customer-specific exceptions (e.g., legal hold) we include a hold marker and keep preservation manifests; we can provide the manifest showing the hold window and PTO.

Suggested SIG/CAIQ language: "Redwood Inference maintains documented telemetry retention defaults and provides signed manifests and audit log excerpts to customers to demonstrate deletion or preservation actions." We'll include a short CAIQ mapping table tying these behaviours back to relevant control IDs.

Kim — if you want I can assemble the artifacts into the ZIP and redact samples; Marissa, please confirm attestation language and signatory.

Ben Carter
Principal Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
